title: 2018 Knox Legal Studies Trial
notes: Text extracted from the multiple-choice pages; shared textual stimulus transcribed as a group.

groups.stimulus: Luke aged 16 and Rick aged 22, planned to rob Jennifer. The next day Luke drove the car, acted as the lookout, and waited for Rick to rob Jennifer. Rick assaulted Jennifer before stealing a few items and then they both drove away.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a mitigating factor at sentencing?
David is the victim of a home invasion and fears for the life of his small children. He kills the offender. Which of the following is the best defence for David?
A person has been detained without charge by the police. What is this an example of?
4 Which of the following orders are not available from the Children’s Court?
Who sets out guideline judgements?
Under what circumstances is a 13 year old girl who is under arrest breaking the law?

options.A: When she runs home to get away from the police
options.B: When she refuses to answer questions by the police
options.C: When she asks the police officer his name
options.D: When she refuses to be strip searched

questions.stem: Who could challenge a juror who has been selected to serve on a jury, causing them to leave the jury and no longer be a part of it?
Under what circumstance would an individual not be entitled to the right to silence at police questioning?

options.A: If they are a young offender
options.D: If they are held on remand

questions.stem: Which party to a crime would Luke be with regard to the charge of robbery?
Which of the following categories of crime best describes Rick’s indictable offence?
Vivienne was found guilty of a series of summary offences. She claims that she is innocent. In which court will Vivienne have her appeal heard?
Freedom from torture and slavery are best protected by the:

options.A: International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights
options.B: International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights

questions.stem: Which of the following must be proven in a strict liability offence?
Which legal instrument protects the right to vote in Australia?
Human rights are said to be inherent. What is the meaning of this?

options.A: That human rights apply to everybody
options.B: That human rights exist from birth
options.C: That human rights cannot be discriminated against due to sex or race
options.D: That human rights cannot be taken away

questions.stem: In the Wik People v Queensland decision which human right was realised for Aboriginal people?

Mary is sentenced to 10 years in prison for a serious criminal offence. The judge in sentencing refers to the fact that this offence is becoming all too common and must be addressed through more significant sentences. What was a significant consideration in Mary’s sentence?
In NSW there is a mandatory life sentence for the murder of a police officer. Which of the following best describes the purpose of punishment for the community?
Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding the Children’s Court in NSW?

options.A: The Children’s Court hears all criminal matters involving offenders under 18 years of age.
options.B: The Children’s Court follows the exact same rules and procedures as all other NSW courts.
options.C: Once a juvenile offender turns 18 they can no longer have their matter heard in the Children’s Court.
options.D: The Children’s Court can sentence offenders to juvenile detention, even if they are over the age of 18.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a feature of victim impact statements in NSW?

options.A: Used by the courts for all indictable offences
options.B: Used by the prosecution to determine evidence
options.C: Used by judges when determining some sentences
options.D: Used by the jury when determining some verdicts
